'''''Huernia schneideriana''''', commonly known as the '''red dragon flower''' or '''medusa hair plant''', is a [[perennial]] [[Succulent plant|succulent]] in the [[dogbane]] and [[Nerium|oleander]] family [[Apocynaceae]], native to [[Tanzania]] in eastern Africa.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=Red Dragon Flower - Huernia schneideriana |url=https://planetdesert.com/products/red-dragon-flower-huernia-schneideriana |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=Planet Desert |language=en}}</ref> The species is a popular houseplant because of its long, cascading leaves, and shallow crimson flowers. Introduced specimens of ''Huernia schneideriana'' have been spotted in [[Mexico]], [[Honduras]], [[Costa Rica]], [[Panama]], [[Venezuela]], [[Ecuador]], [[Brazil]], and [[India]].<ref name=":0">A.Berger [[Monatsschrift für Kakteenkunde]] 23: 177 (1913)</ref><ref name="Albers-2002">Albers, F. & Meve, U. (eds.) (2002). Illustrated handbook of succulent plants Asclepiadaceae, corr. 2nd printing: 1-318. Springer, Berlin, Heidelberg, New York.</ref><ref name="Goyder-2012">Goyder, S., Harris, T., Masinde, S., Meve, U. & Venter, J. (2012). Flora of Tropical East Africa, Apocynaceae(2): 1-530.</ref>

== Description ==
''Huernia schneideriana'' grows in a clumping manner with smooth, square stems that can be green to reddish, depending on sun exposure. These stems, which are typically {{cvt|2 to 6|in}} long, but are able to grow up to 30 inches long, are lined with soft tooth-like [[tubercle]]s that are rigid, but not very sharp.<ref name=":1" /> The [[flower]]s are small, funnel-shaped, and grow on short pedicels from the base of the stems.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web |last=WoS |date=2018-07-28 |title=Huernia schneideriana (Red Dragon Flower) |url=https://worldofsucculents.com/huernia-schneideriana-red-dragon-flower/ |access-date=2025-09-17 |website=World of Succulents |language=en-US}}</ref> They are typically a dark crimson or burgundy color with a velvety texture, and they often have a darker central ring. The flower petals are fused at the base, forming a funnel, and then spread outwards. A unique characteristic of the flowers is their lack of the characteristic rotting-meat odor, common in many other ''Huernia'' species that are pollinated by flies and beetles.<ref name=":2" />

[[File:Very old hernia schneiderania.jpg|thumb|On very old specimens, stems can get to lengths of up to 30 inches]]

== Taxonomy and etymology ==
[[File:Hernia schneideriana flower.jpg|thumb|Close up of flower.]]
''Huernia schneideriana'' was originally described by a botanist from Germany, [[Alwin Berger]] in 1913.<ref name=":0" /> For a somewhat long time, ''Huernia schneideriana'' was thought to be a natural hybrid of ''[[Huernia verekeri]]'' and ''[[Huernia aspera]],'' but is now known as a distinct, unique species. The genus "''Huernia''" is a contribution to [[Johannes Heurnius]], a Dutch botanist, physician, and missionary. Heurnius was recognized as one of the first Europeans to acquire and document plants from [[Cape of Good Hope]], [[South Africa]]. The species' name was misspelled when the genus ''Huernia'' was formally described.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Peterson |first=Lillian |date=2020-11-19 |title=Garden Club of Cape Coral |url=https://www.gardenclubofcapecoral.com/ |access-date=2025-09-17 |language=en-US}}</ref> The epithet honors [[Camillo Karl Schneider]].<ref>A. Berger, Heurnia Schneideriana Berger spec. nov. Eine neue Stapeliee aus Deutsch-Ostafrika. Monatsschrift für Kakteenkunde. vol. 23. page 177</ref>

== Uses ==
[[File:Huernia schneideriana - Talcott Greenhouse - Mount Holyoke College - DSC04546.JPG|thumb|Potted in a [[greenhouse]] alongside other species in the genus.]]

The most common use of ''Huernia schneideriana'' is as a decorative plant. ''Huernia schneideriana'' is an ideal houseplant for bright indoor locations and can be grown outdoors in suitable climates (USDA hardiness zones 9-11).<ref name=":6">{{Cite web |title=Red Dragon Flower, Schneider's Huernia - Red Flowers or Flower Parts - Almost Eden |url=https://www.almostedenplants.com/shopping/products/12242-red-dragon-flower-schneiders-huernia/ |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=www.almostedenplants.com}}</ref> The unique stems and flowers of ''Huernia schneideriana'' make it an interesting conversation piece and a popular choice for succulent collections.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Huernia schneideriana {{!}} plant lust |url=https://plantlust.com/plants/32451/huernia-schneideriana/ |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=plantlust.com}}</ref> In its native region, the stems of some ''Huernia'' species were allegedly boiled eaten as a [[famine food]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=by |first=Written |date=2018-11-29 |title=Huernia schneideriana A.k.a Red Dragon Flower Care and Information |url=https://crazycrittersinc.com/huernia-schneideriana-a-k-a-red-dragon-flower-care-and-information/plant-and-garden/ |access-date=2025-09-18 |website=Crazy Plants Crazy Critters |language=en-US}}</ref> However, this is not a common or recommended practice due to the plant's uncommon and nutrient-poor nature.
